coaching.headline: Seven fights won and six cashed; they won two and cashed zero — this win was conversion, not just kills.
coaching.team: The pattern to keep: fight on top of a prize, then take it. We out-hit them on objectives 61583 to 11282, went 8-4 on towers, and took seven picks on enemies caught rotating alone while giving back only three. The close was clinical — Orb Prime at 28, Genesis Core at 29, Primal Fangtooth at 30, core down at 32. What a better team punishes: both fights we lost were the same two-man shape — Zarus and Murdock into Grux's pull at 7.9, then into Wraith and Legion at 13.8 — with three teammates still in lane and our support pinned in a losing matchup, the film flags three of us with no armor against Adele's 28k physical, and the 5v4 at 23.7 still went only 2-2 and cost an outer tower.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: Fangtooth control. They lifted Fangtooth across the map at 14 and 21 — the first behind winning the 13.8 fight outright, the second a straight body-for-objective trade while losing the 20.9 fight 0-3 at their own pit, our only won fight left uncashed. From there we stopped leaving prizes on the table: the 3-0 river fight at 27.1 rolled into Orb Prime at 28, Genesis Core at 29 and Primal Fangtooth at 30, and the 4-0 stand at our inhibitor at 31.3 ended it. Four anti-heal items into the Adele-plus-Mourn double-heal comp is why the late fights went 4-0 and 2-0 instead of coin flips.

perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Mr_Meat31 was the engine: 11 kills and Mourn dead to him six times, which removed the enemy's pull-and-sustain support before the brawls even formed. The leak: four deaths, three of them in the same shape — two-man skirmishes alongside Zarus at 7.9, 10.5 and 13.8 while mid, offlane and support were all still in lane. The same aggression one beat later, after the shove-and-rotate arrives, turns those coin flips into the 3-0s and 4-0s the team ran in the second half.
perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Goldilocks324 turned in the cleanest film on either team: 8/0/4 with zero deaths, and the solo 2-0 on Grux and Wraith at our Fangtooth at 7.3 that set the early tempo. The add: both lost skirmishes (7.9 and 13.8) happened while Gideon was ahead in mid and absent — on this film a shove-and-rotate from mid flips a 0-2 into a numbers advantage. A won lane is a ticket to someone else's fight; punch it earlier.
perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Cuban Noobster turned a lost lane into a winning map: Mourn owned the support matchup on paper all game, yet the film shows kills on Grux at 20.9 and 24.1, the closing kill on Adele at 31.8, 10 assists and a single death. The habit to fix before a stronger team collects: no armor into a three-physical comp — the caught-out death to Legion at 3.7, alone and outside any fight, is what that costs.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Willy Guggenheim won the jungle and the map: 7/2/8, a team-best 18743 objective damage, 8 wards, and Grux dead to him at 9.5, 17 and 27.4. Both deaths were the same call — two-man fights alongside Murdock at 7.9 and 13.8 with mid, offlane and support all elsewhere. The 7.9 loss bought our Fangtooth in the same window, so it reads as a trade; 13.8 at their pit bought nothing. The timing fix: start those fights after the rotation is already moving, not before — and against 28k of Adele physical, some armor next time; the film flags him among three of us with none.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: The film's lane read scored the offlane ours all game against Adele — a paper verdict the 1/5 scoreline never cashed — but the 19.3 kill on her in the 2-0 at our tower plus six assists show the engage-and-brawl plan worked. The deaths were the tax: first blood at 2.4, caught alone by Grux at 4.6 and again at 18.1, and the 23.7 death that directly preceded their outer tower at 23.9 — the only death on this film with a listed cost. Against a Grux jungle the sidelane rule is simple: no extended trades without vision of him. The build compounded it — none of the Overlord, Rapture, Cursed Scroll core came online, and no armor against three physical damage dealers.

threats: Chain-CC risk (2 hard-CC abilities, ~1.0s of lockdown): Mourn Abduct (pull), Grux Crush (knockup 0.5s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Heal-stacking: Adele, Mourn. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought none.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Bayle Kingslayer (knockback). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Zinx) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Static Trap root → Buckshot → Hot Pursuit AS → Long Arm of the Law global snipe
ourKits.winCondition: trap for the root, then out-range with Shots Fired and finish with the global ult
ourKits.passive: every 5th basic is a long-range bonus shot
ourKits.playWith: frontline/peel to protect his low mobility
ourKits.playAgainst: almost no escape — engage past the trap and he dies

ourKits.combo: Void Breach slow → Cosmic Rift → Black Hole on the grouped enemies
ourKits.winCondition: land Black Hole / Cosmic Rift on a clumped team for AoE burst
ourKits.passive: an ability-empowered basic tethers a target for bonus damage
ourKits.playWith: hard engage that clumps enemies into his Black Hole
ourKits.playAgainst: immobile with long cooldowns — dodge the skillshots and dive him once Black Hole is down

ourKits.combo: Ricochet stun → Bad Medicine zone → Infuse heal an ally → Neural Regenesis revive
ourKits.winCondition: keep an ally alive with Infuse + the revive ult and poke with Ricochet
ourKits.playWith: a carry she can pocket-heal and revive
ourKits.playAgainst: she can't heal herself — dive HER; bait the revive before committing

ourKits.combo: Evade in → Barricade block → Spear of Nyr (execute <20%) → Coliseum ult arena
ourKits.winCondition: trap a target in Coliseum and out-duel with stacked Gladiator
ourKits.playWith: a team that joins him inside the Coliseum
ourKits.playAgainst: don't fight him in his arena — disengage; burst through Barricade's window

ourKits.combo: Skull Crusher gap-close → Dire Howl slow → Cursed Edge → Kingslayer knockback dash, Berserk at low HP
ourKits.winCondition: engage, drop low into Berserk and out-brawl
ourKits.playWith: follow-up while he commits the dive
ourKits.playAgainst: his Berserk rewards low HP — burst him fully or disengage; anti-heal helps

enemyKits.combo: Peekaboo! mark+slow → Knock, Knock! sniper → Back It Up! displacement ult
enemyKits.winCondition: land long-range snipes on marked targets and reset on takedowns
enemyKits.playWith: engage that holds a target in his sniper line
enemyKits.playAgainst: close the gap — he's weak point-blank; dodge the skillshot snipe

enemyKits.combo: Abduct pull → Contagion ally-heal bugs → Beguile damage-reduction → Eclipse vision-denial ult
enemyKits.winCondition: pull a target in and sustain the team through the brawl
enemyKits.playWith: burst that punishes his pulled target
enemyKits.playAgainst: respect the long Abduct channel/range; anti-heal blunts Contagion

enemyKits.combo: Smash 'n Grab pull → Crush knockup → Warlord's Challenge stun → bleed-stacked basics
enemyKits.winCondition: land the pull→knockup chain to lock a target while bleed and AS shred them
enemyKits.passive: basics stack a bleed for sustained damage
enemyKits.playWith: follow-up burst inside his knockup/stun window
enemyKits.playAgainst: telegraphed engage — bait Crush/Pull, then punish; kite his slow start
